thread:
billing-bot: New invoice uploaded: INV-2026-03-47 (uploaded to finance bucket). File: gs://redwood-billing/invoices/INV-2026-03-47.json :receipt: 

alex: saw this in the morning — invoice total is ~6% higher than forecast. there is a weird line: 'Reservation Rate Adjustment - GPU' for $28,400. not sure what that is. anyone else see it?

maria_fin: yep opened it. looks like a negative credit was reversed and a separate 'Accelerator Retroactive Surcharge' appeared. lines: 
```
Invoice Line: Accelerator Retroactive Surcharge (asia-east2) - $31,200
Invoice Line: Committed Use Discount Adjustment (GPU) - -$2,800
```

lina_ops: hmm. our reserved capacity commitments for april were stable. I just ran the reservation report and showing 100% of reserved vGPUs in use for the month window we expected. can we confirm timeline?

sam_irving: querying billing export now against invoice id. running bq: 
```
 bq query --nouse_legacy_sql '
 SELECT invoice_id, sku_description, amount, start_time, end_time
 FROM `company-billing.gcp_invoice.invoice_items`
 WHERE invoice_id = "INV-2026-03-47"
 ORDER BY amount DESC
'
```

sam_irving: results show two entries that look duplicate-ish: Accelerator Premium Support (asia-east2) for $15,600 and Accelerator Premium (asia-east2) for $15,600 — same sku_description variants and identical usage start/end. looks like a labeling shuffle doubled the charge.

alex: could be a retroactive rate change + CUD adjustment. but double identical lines suggests the billing pipeline may have appended both original and adjusted lines instead of netting them. is the CUD external adjustment negative matching the surcharge? math doesn't add up.

maria_fin: net delta for those three lines = $31,200 - $2,800 = $28,400 which matches the anomaly number. but the duplicated premium lines add another $15,600 -> pushes it higher.

lina_ops: I pulled our reservations usage from the reservation service: reservation_id: rsv-14c3, window: 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28, reserved_count: 48 A100s, actual_bound: 47. Looks like one GPU was unbound for a short period and we had an autoscale fallback to on-demand for ~6 hours on 2/17 (logs: infra/allocations/2026-02-17.log). That shouldn't produce a $30k delta.

alex: ok next steps: 1) confirm whether cloud retroactive price change applied globally for that billing cycle, 2) check whether invoice export pipeline produced duplicate rows, 3) open case with cloud support if we can't reconcile. Who owns #1?

maria_fin: I'll flag with cloud finance contacts and check the published rate-change bulletin. also will reconcile with our committed-use discount report.

sam_irving: filing a lightweight internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BI-5219 with the bq query snapshot and invoice lines. tagging @cloud-support-bot to see if there's an automated status.

cloud-support-bot: Case created with cloud provider (case123456). Initial reply expected within 48 hours. Reference: INV-2026-03-47 / billing export id gcp_export_202603.

lina_ops: I also ran a checksum against our copy of the exported CSV vs the BigQuery "invoice_items" table. checksum mismatch for 7 rows in asia-east2: seems like duplicate insert events with different event_id. snippet: 
```
INSERT id: 9876abc, sku: Accelerator Premium, amount: 15600
INSERT id: 9876abc-dup, sku: Accelerator Premium, amount: 15600
```

alex: that points to a pipeline bug. sam, can you and infra/etl check the export job that writes to BigQuery? maybe retry dedupe and re-run ingestion to verify.

sam_irving: will do. spinning up a job to reprocess invoice file with dedupe on invoice_line_id and will post results here. ETA 2 hours.

maria_fin: if reprocessing still shows net $28.4k unexpected, we need to prepare a finance note and hold cash until cloud support responds. please include impact to committed capacity KPIs.

lina_ops: quick note: our alerts show no sustained shortage; this looks like billing-side bookkeeping rather than consumption. but we should double-check any region failovers that could trigger premium.

alex: agreed. thanks all. Sam — ping when reprocess done. Maria — compile initial reconciliations. Lina — check allocation logs around 2/17 for any anomalies. I'll draft a short incident-style note for execs if this becomes material. :white_check_mark: 

[some time later]

sam_irving: reprocessed with dedupe: duplicates removed, invoice_items table adjusted, net invoice variance reduced from +$43,200 to +$27,400. still a $27.4k unexplained delta (mostly the Accelerator Retroactive Surcharge).

maria_fin: attached reconciliation spreadsheet to BI-5219. raising this to P2 with accounting.

alex: good troubleshooting — filing follow-up to see if cloud retroactive pricing policy caused the surcharge. if cloud confirms policy we may seek an adjustment or credit. otherwise we'll need to absorb and update forecast.

lina_ops: will keep monitoring cluster allocations; nothing else suspicious so far.

cloud-support-bot: Cloud support responded: initial triage — a region-wide retroactive rate recalculation was applied due to a vendor invoice correction. They are reviewing whether duplicate export rows were side-effect. Estimated time to final response: 3 business days.

alex: thanks. keep this thread updated. if we get a credit we can close BI-5219, if not finance will decide next steps.
